content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper proposes Adaptive Anchors for keypoint localization tasks. While the previous uses fixed anchors, the method finds anchors adaptively for keypoint localization. The method noticeably works well on multiple keypoint localization tasks compared to the baselines.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Motivation and intuition are straightforward and easy to understand.

While the proposed idea is simple, it could improve the baselines on several benchmarks. Especially, the method works well on multiple keypoint localization tasks. However, the paper should also analyze why the method does not show significant improvements in single-person pose estimation. 

The paper claims the proposed method improves confidence. It is not clear the benefit of having higher confidence. Does it also encourage confident wrong predictions? It should be analyzed carefully.

The main concern is that the method is not applied to state-of-the-art methods and architectures. Therefore, it is not clear whether the proposed method can achieve state-of-the-art performances and contributes to the research community.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The paper is well-written and easy to understand. The paper also proposes an adaptive anchor which was not explored before. 
In Figs. 1 and 4, it will be better to show the actually estimated key points too.
content.summary_of_the_review: While the method improves the baselines compared to the fixed anchor, the proposed method was not applied to the state-of-the-art methods. Therefore it is still not clear whether the proposed method can be generalizable to recent architectures or methods.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a new keypoint localization pipeline. Existing key point localization is achieved by either producing a confidence heatmap and selecting points among high-scoring pixels or regressing the offset from a pre-defined anchor point. The former usually yields accurate results but suffers occlusion parts; the latter is robust to the invisible part but struggles with long-distance dependence. This paper proposes a new framework combining the advantages of the previous methods that can infer invisible regions while keeping a good accurate localization.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Pros:
- The proposed framework is simple and effective, as demonstrated in various tasks.

Cons:
- In terms of an invisible key point, the paper claims it can adaptively infer the candidate anchors near the occluded pixels before refinement. More details or motivations need to be included regarding the anchor selection module. (e.g. Discussion on how the selection component learns the implicit relationship between the visible prior and the invisible detection.)
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The proposed pipeline is straightforward. In terms of novelty, the paper may need more discussion and comparison to some current detection works. For example, some detection framework like Yolo treats each patch as the anchor and then refines it by regressing the offset. Besides, this method builds a candidate pool from a feature map and produces the anchor local refinement. What is the time & memory efficiency compared with others?
content.summary_of_the_review: Regarding my concerns over the technique novelty, I would like to rate this paper around the borderline. More discussions of motivation and comparison to other similar works can be included to consolidate the claimed novelty.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper studied the problem of keypoint localization, however, it looks like not new as the presented method extensively relies on anchor-based classification and regression. To my knowledge, anchor-based methods have been extensively studied since Faster-RCNN and I did not get any new message from this paper.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Weaknesses:
1. The novelty is very limited. The presented method looks like reinventing the wheels that have been used for many years in the computer vision community. For example, the concept of the anchor has been well-studied since the emergence of Faster-RCNN. For the problem of human pose estimation, there have also been a number of studies that take inspiration from the "anchor".  Therefore, it is hard to say that the proposed method is new in 2022.

2. The experiments are not convincing. 
    2.1. What is **single keypoint** localization on COCO? To the best of my knowledge, the keypoint annotations in the COCO dataset are about the human pose. Suppose the input image contains only one person, how could we define a single keypoint in such a case? Furthermore, how could we define the invisible keypoints as you mentioned in Table 2? For the keypoint annotations in the COCO dataset, some keypoints with zero visibility are not reliable, which would make the experimental results unconvincing. 
    2.2. The experimental results on the multi-person pose estimation are not good as the associative embedding, which weakens the contributions of this paper.
    2.3. The performance of the presented method is far away from the state of the arts. For example, the average precision of multi-person pose estimation has been more than 70% on the COCO dataset, but the presented method only achieves an AP of 50.5%.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: As I mentioned in the "Strength And Weaknesses", this paper did neither have any significant novelty, nor convincing experimental results.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper contains flaws in both the methodological contributions and the experimental results. Thus, it should not be accepted.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
This paper proposes to detect an adaptive anchor (AdaAnchor) for keypoint localization. 

The main contribution to fuse the localization confidence and accuracy to compute the anchor score (Eq.9).

Experiments on  single keypoint localization task and multiple keypoint localization task show the effectiveness of the proposed method.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
[Strength]
1. This paper is well-written and easy to follow. It is very friendly for readers.
2. Though the proposed method is simple, it is very effective for both single keypoint localization and multiple keypoint localization tasks. 
3. The main contribution is fusing localization confidence and accuracy with a Gaussian kernel. I'm surprised by this simple fusing method if no one has exploited it before.

[Weaknesses]
I cannot find major weaknesses and only have minor comments.

1. Eq.8. It seems that the hyberparameter $\sigma $ depends on the size of feature map. How to handle input image size with different resolution？

2. Local Refinement.
The description of the proposed local refinement module is blurry. 

Can we only use the same coarse branch with more parameters (amount to the refinement branch) to achieve the same performance as Eq.12?
content.summary_of_the_review: A simple fusion method is proposed to combine localization confidence and accuracy to predict better keypoints.

content.title: Adaptive Anchor for Robust Keypoint Localization
content.abstract: Existing keypoint localization methods mostly select pre-defined points like image center as anchors, then infer keypoint locations referring to anchors. Pre-defined anchors are sensitive to occlusions and crowded scenes, leading to degraded robustness. This paper proposes to detect Adaptive Anchor (AdaAnchor) for keypoint localization. Instead of relying on pre-defined rules, AdaAnchor is adaptively selected by maximizing both the keypoint localization confidence and accuracy. This strategy leads to more robust keypoint localization even with the existence of occlusions and truncations. AdaAnchor can be flexibly integrated into different methods by replacing their anchor point selection strategies. Experiments show that it surpasses previous anchor selection methods on both single and multiple keypoint localization tasks. For instance, replacing the heatmap-anchor with AdaAnchor reduces the localization error of invisible keypoints by 6%, meanwhile improves the confidence by 41.7+% on COCO in single keypoint localization. This advantage sustains on multiple keypoint localization task, e.g., AdaAnchor outperforms heatmap-anchor by 4.8% AP on bottom-up multi-person pose estimation.
